catalog_quote: Word stress in Sahu-Padisua is phonemic. Although the place of word stress is not predictable there is a preference for certain stress patterns. Thus one finds that most often the first syllable is stressed in monomorphemic words of two and three syllables, and the antepenultimate syllable in monomorphemic words of four syllables and more. Stress on the penultimate syllable of three- and four-syllable words is not uncommon. Least often one finds stress on the final syllable. Most of these words have been identified as loanwords. It is noteworthy that the equivalent word in the source language does not necessarily has the stress on the last syllable. The place of the stress is not affected by affixation or reduplication. (Visser & Voorhoeve 1987)

sources.quote: p.83: 'In Sahu, stress is normally a compound of intensity and length but can also have a frequency (pitch) component... The stress rules have not been fully determined yet, but only one example has been elicited where stress seems to be the only contrastive feature.
